summary: Hooks night for Craze & Crash: compared question and claim titles inside each channel of the niche scan and our own six Shorts' openings, added that evidence to two waiting challengers, and added 3 sourced Short topics (Toys R Us's 735 stores, Sears's mail-order houses, Kodak's $1 Brownie).
why: The feed had only 9 open Short topics (about 4-5 days at 2 a day). In the scan, the closest business channels' question titles get 0.71-0.92x their claim titles, so the claim champion stays. Our two object-first paradox openings (Stanley 1,139, Tamagotchi 764) out-viewed the deal-first ones (12-46), though there's no stayed-to-watch data yet.

findings.title: Question titles don't beat claims in our niche
findings.detail: Within-channel, English Shorts under 90 days: Rise Fall Repeat 0.71x, Ravate 0.73x, Signal 404 0.77x; median of 19 channels 1.09x; 3x+ breakout share 23% vs 22%.

findings.title: Our object-first openings out-viewed deal-first ones
findings.detail: Stanley's cup 1,139 and Tamagotchi 764 against the $35 Swoosh 12, Nokia/Microsoft 46, Dollar Shave Club 38. Views only; Analytics shows 0 engaged views so far.

findings.title: Sears's 'How Sears was built' Short broke out
findings.detail: 90K on 19.9K (4.5x) at Rise Fall Repeat; became a sourced Sears mail-order-house topic.

findings.title: New Coke Shorts flop in the scan
findings.detail: 524, 2,184 and 552 views; kept as a long topic only.

changes.title: 3 Short topics added to the feed
Evidence added to doc-short-question-hook and doc-document-first
changes.detail: No new challenger; both leanings favour the current champion.
